text: Sajood Sailani, born Ghulam Mohammed Wani in 1936 in Dalgate Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, was a Kashmiri playwright, painter, theater artist, cartoonist, and poet. He is primarily known for his radio plays written in regional languages, producing about 150 radio plays, 27 stage dramas, and 40 comedies throughout his career. His work was primarily in Urdu and Kashmiri, and he gained recognition for the play Kaej Raath (Dumb Night), which earned him the Sahitya Akademi Award under the Kashmiri category in 1994. He served on the Sahitya Akademi advisory board from 1973 to 1977 and again in 1990. He began his career while studying in the 10th class and never attended college for further studies. Inspired by All India Radio's night show Hawa Mahal, he started writing short sketch comedies and later worked for Radio Kashmir Srinagar (modern-day AIR Srinagar), where he produced many of his literary works, including prominent dramas such as Kaej Raath, Gaashe Taaruk (Guiding Star), Ropye Rood (Money Shower), Zalur (Spider), Vutri binyul (Catastrophe), Fundbaz (Swindler), and Tentykor (Catgut). He also recorded nohakhwaani (the tragedy of Husayn ibn Ali) and wrote scripts of noha depicting the battle of Karbala. As a painter, he established the Wani Art Gallery and received an uncertain cultural award from the government of Jammu and Kashmir's Department of Cultural Academy in 1970. He is sometimes regarded as the only Kashmiri writer in the 20th century to have written a radio play in Bhojpuri. He was suffering from a chronic condition for several years and passed away on 17 November 2020 in Zafran Colony, Srinagar, and is buried in Pandrethan cemetery, Srinagar. He is survived by three children, including two sons—Showkat Shehri (playwright and writer) and Manzoor Ahmad (psychiatrist)—and a daughter.
